recommendations.reason: The Connector map lets us choose a short trip between market, park, and downtown. I’d leave time to linger at your favorite stop.
Some Dayton aviation stops suit a transit-first day; others need another ride. Let’s sort out the journey before choosing our favorites.

blocks.text: Cincinnati’s market, or Dayton’s aviation story? Oh, you don’t have to fit both into today. Tell me the one place you’re most excited about, and we’ll build around it. I like a plan with room for a seat, something to eat, and the occasional ‘ooh, what’s over there?’ ♡

I’d plan these two days differently. Cincinnati’s central Connector loop lets us choose a stop and decide later about another. Dayton’s aviation sites spread across the city and Wright-Patterson area, so transport needs more thought. Either way, let’s pick one place you really want to see, then leave the extras to energy, service, and opening hours.

For a shorter Cincinnati day, I’d begin at Findlay Market and ride to Washington Park. The city map lists Findlay Market–Race as station 12, Liberty & Race as 13, Washington Park as 14, Public Library as 16, Fountain Square as 18, and The Banks as 1. That gives us choices from Over-the-Rhine toward downtown and the riverfront. We can stop at the park or continue if it sounds lovely. Nobody’s grading us on finishing the loop.

blocks.text: The Connector has level boarding, while sidewalks and destination entrances need their own check. I’d choose a rest stop before adding another leg. A plan should leave us enough energy to enjoy where we are.
blocks.title: Leave room for a pause

blocks.text: The Connector is fare-free; the city describes level boarding and audio and visual stop information. That doesn’t tell us everything about the sidewalks, curbs, market aisles, or entrances afterward. If you want less walking, I’d ride between stations and spend longer at one place. If a market browse and park walk suit you, we can do that and decide about more later.

blocks.title: Dayton: Wright-Dunbar and the spaces between
blocks.eyebrow: Two to three hours or a full day

blocks.text: For a transit-first Dayton visit, I’d begin at Wright-Dunbar. NPS identifies the nearest Greater Dayton RTA stop at West Third and Williams. The Interpretive Center is at 16 South Williams Street, beside the Wright Cycle Company building at 22. NPS places the Paul Laurence Dunbar House three blocks west along Third and three north on Paul Laurence Dunbar Street; check its schedule before walking over. Its accessibility page lists an elevator, accessible restrooms, benches, a Cycle Company ramp, film captions and audio description, and typed communication equipment at the visitor center. Those are useful details to have before we choose our stops.

blocks.text: For a fuller day, I’d eat and rest downtown before a separate ride to Huffman Prairie and the National Museum of the U.S. Air Force. NPS says there’s no public transit to the Huffman Prairie visitor center. Use RTA’s trip planner for Wright-Dunbar and check your date’s route; don’t expect that bus leg to cover everything. Staying downtown longer is a perfectly lovely alternative if you’d prefer fewer transfers.

blocks.title: Match the route to your time and mobility

items.label: Short Cincinnati visit
items.text: Ride from Findlay Market to Washington Park, take a seated break, and decide whether to continue downtown.

items.label: Long Cincinnati visit
items.text: Use the published station order toward the Public Library, Fountain Square, or The Banks; leave time between stops.

items.label: Short Dayton visit
items.text: Use RTA to reach Wright-Dunbar and focus on the visitor center and Cycle Company; confirm current hours.

items.label: Long Dayton visit
items.text: Arrange separate transportation to Huffman Prairie and the Air Force museum; NPS reports no public transit to Huffman Prairie.

items.label: Access planning
items.text: The Connector’s boarding features describe the vehicle, while Metro Access has separate eligibility, service-area, and scheduling rules. Ask the operator about your journey.

blocks.text: My favorite kind of route leaves us time to notice something and change our minds. Check alerts, hours, and access arrangements for your date. Cincinnati gives us several stopping points along a loop; Dayton asks us to plan between spread-out sites. There, a little preparation—and more room to enjoy where we are.
A little looking, a little sitting, permission to change your mind. That’s your day in Ohio. I’m happy we found a beginning together. ♡
